hypothesis: For elementary rules 60 and 188 started from a single black cell, the colour of the cell at position x after t steps is a 2-automatic function of (t, x): a fixed finite automaton reading the base-2 digits of t and x in parallel (one digit pair per step, hence about log2(t) steps) outputs the colour, and this automaton can be constructed from the pattern and reproduces it exactly, including at times not used in its construction.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered, for each of rules 60 and 188: (i) the number of distinct 2-kernel elements A(2^k t + r, 2^k x + s), compared on a 64 x 64 window, saturates: the cumulative count over levels k <= 5 equals the cumulative count over all levels k <= K - 6 of a 2^K x 2^K pattern with K = 11 (i.e. no new element appears beyond level 5), and that count is at most 64; (ii) the finite automaton whose states are those kernel elements and whose transitions on a digit pair (dt, dx) go from element (k, r, s) to (k+1, r + 2^k dt, s + 2^k dx) is consistent (every representative of a state yields the same target state for each digit pair) and, run on the least-significant-first binary digits of (t, x), reproduces 100% of the cells of an independently evolved 2^12 x 2^12 pattern (t < 4096), three quarters of which lie outside the K = 11 construction range; (iii) the number of automaton steps for a cell at time t equals the number of binary digits of t, i.e. floor(log2 t) + 1.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered: for rule 60 or rule 188 the kernel count keeps growing beyond level 5 (no saturation) or exceeds 64, or the automaton is inconsistent, or any cell of the 2^12 x 2^12 pattern disagrees with the automaton's output. Control rules 30 and 110 (not nested) are expected to fail (i) and (ii); if they passed, the test would be too weak and the verdict would be 'inconclusive' with reason 'not-operationalizable'.
interpretation: Wolfram's statement (p. 744) is that the colour of a cell of rule 60 or rule 188 after t steps can be found by a cellular automaton acting on the base-2 digit sequences of the cell's coordinates (6 colours for rule 60, 12 for rule 188) in about log2(t) steps instead of t steps. The finite-automaton formulation used here is equivalent: a two-dimensional pattern computable from the binary digits of (t, x) by a finite-state device is a 2-automatic double sequence, whose characterization (Cobham, Salon) is finiteness of its 2-kernel; the automaton's step count is the number of digit pairs, floor(log2 t) + 1. The exact state counts Wolfram quotes (6 and 12) refer to his particular digit-CA encoding and are not tested; only the existence of a finite digit automaton and its logarithmic step count are. Rules 60 and 188 both grow only to the right from a single black cell at x = 0, so A(t, x) is defined for 0 <= x <= t and taken as 0 for x > t. For the controls, the right half (x >= 0) of rule 30, 90 and 150 and the mirror image of rule 110 are used. The clause 'nested patterns generally' is addressed only through rules 90 and 150 as further nested examples.

datasets.name: Elementary rules 60 and 188 from a single black cell, 4096 steps, 4096 columns (generated by analysis.py)
datasets.program_family: elementary cellular automata, Wolfram rule numbering; initial condition single black cell at x = 0 on a white line, fixed white boundary far to the right (never reached) and at x = -1 (the pattern never spreads left for these rules, asserted); array A[t][x], t, x in 0..4095; the automaton is built from A[t, x < 2048] and tested on the whole array
datasets.role: the two patterns named in the claim

datasets.name: Elementary rules 30, 110 (mirrored), 90 and 150 from a single black cell, 4096 steps, right half x >= 0 (generated by analysis.py)
datasets.program_family: as above on a two-sided line; A[t][x] = colour at x >= 0; rule 110 is run with left and right swapped so that its pattern grows to the right
datasets.role: negative controls (30, 110) and further nested examples (90, 150); not part of the verdict
